decision: Can prior returned errors identify a class losing recall under the strong fixed source-plus-site logistic model and restore it by changing its class scores? A locally designed recall correction, not a claim of a novel algorithm or a known impact. Freeze before fetching UCI 487. Official and UCI 322 were previously studied.
method: Start with the identical fixed mixed classifier. When predicting each selected feedback row, keep the unmodified mixed model scores and the calibrated observer's class from before the true label, independent of which arm was deployed. For each true class compare cumulative correctness of mixed vs observer. Mark a class only after five old examples of that class, if observer has rescued at least two more than mixed and its observed recall is at least .02 higher. For each marked class estimate the smallest nonnegative margin addition that recovers enough previous true-class mixed scores to meet observer recall minus .02: quantile of log(top alternative probability / true-class probability), tie handling deterministic, clamp to log(4). Other class offsets remain zero. Fixed candidates: unmodified mixed and observer; fixed contrasts: apply the same margin estimator with target recall 0.95 to every class with five examples (ignore observer), and freeze the first nonzero warned offsets. One extra control, on any warning use the whole observer instead of changing mixed scores. No fitting of a new prediction network, no future labels or dataset-specific thresholds. Marked-class maxima may sacrifice precision; score net benefits on subsequent accepted batches, not the old labels.
independent: UCI 487 temperature modulation, previously unused source; source first three measurement dates in filename order, rest serve in whole date batches. Task is CO concentration band, cut at 5 and 15 ppm (low <=5, high >15, medium otherwise). For each date use 900-second intervals relative to its initial raw timestamp, starting after the first 900-second chamber purge. Only full intervals to the last timestamp within one nominal sampling interval. One prediction per 15-minute exposure window, input 14 sensor means across that window, label band from the median CO level. Exclude any window with no finite reading on at least one sensor or no finite CO target. Report exclusions and random-background clustering at day level. Test two predefined paths: prior dates with all 14 channels for later dates of the same device; and physical replacement using FIGARO R1-R3 as three input channels on the first three dates and FIGARO R4-R6 in the same positions on disjoint subsequent dates. No dates, concentration, humidity, flow, heater voltage or device ID as model inputs. Shared days and labels between the two paths are not independent replications.
conditions: All modes have same source data, predictor set, source classifier bank, equal feedback (up to 32 per day, post-delivery seed 17; no feedback after last day), fit allowance and segregated output. Reuse prior official/322 controls if identical predictions and feedback IDs are checked. Include fixed strong competitors, ongoing and recent-backtest under the common field entry. Report source static leaders too. Score pooled Macro-F1 and minimum true-class recall, each day's signed wins/losses for corrected versus mixed, previous feedback opportunities, number of flags, first valid warning, false alarms, added fits/cost. Use control with same restored inputs. Gate .01 Macro-F1 improvement over all strong controls and no more than .02 worst recall loss, plus actual improvement in the previously harmed class where one was observed. If gate fails do not change default, regardless of development scores. Original H-LLM is a separate classification comparator when run, recent-backtest is strictly a closed-menu adaptation.
